items.title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
items.summary_1line: AI systems become more useful when they can adapt to the people using them, but in multi-agent systems, useful context learned by one agent often remains unavailable to others. We present kernel-managed shared memory,...

items.title: Show HN: Open-source shared memory for teams of AI coding agents
items.summary_1line: Show HN: Open-source shared memory for teams of AI coding agents
items.editor_note: First open-source implementation targeting team-shared agent memory.

editorial.tldr: In early September a startup and an academic paper both proposed giving AI agents persistent, shared memory instead of siloed per-session context. The pitch: context one agent learns should stay usable by every other agent on the same team, not vanish when a session ends.
editorial.whats_new: Motif open-sourced a shared, versioned memory store for teams of coding agents on Sept 21, following MemHub's commercial persistent-memory product and a kernel-managed-memory research paper earlier in the month.
editorial.why_it_matters: If cross-agent shared memory catches on, plan for memory-consistency and access-control problems, not just context loss — evaluate write conflicts before adopting a shared store.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adopting a shared-memory layer for a multi-agent team, test how it handles concurrent writes and stale reads — none of September's three releases publish a consistency model.
